text.p: Mother Teresa's doctor said on Friday that the 86-year-old nun's condition had improved since she was admitted to hospital suffering heart failure.
"Her recovery is satisfactory and she has improved a lot since last night," Dr Asim Kumar Bardhan, the 86-year-old nun's cardiologist told reporters at Calcutta's Woodland nursing home.
"She is not critical. She had liquid diet today," he said.
Bardhan said on Friday afternoon that the Roman Catholic missionary was conscious and breathing on her own, and added that he was hopeful she would recover.
The hospital earlier released a medical bulletin which said she was admitted at 2:30 a.m. (2100 GMT Thursday) with acute left ventricular heart failure.
The state chief of West Bengal, Jyoti Basu, visited her in hospital on Friday.
"She looks cheerful and she is all right," Basu said.
Mother Teresa is revered as the "Saint of the Gutters" for her work with India's destitute.
It was the third time since August that the nun, who won the 1979 Nobel Peace prize, had been admitted to hospital for emergency care.
